scope: Public, user-supplied ISO, executable, manifest, package, archive, and media parser boundaries. All named corpora are source-owned synthetic bytes.

surfaces.max_input: One 2048-byte PVD sector and up to 512 KiB per directory lookup; the containing ISO file itself has no campaign-level byte cap.
surfaces.tables_nesting: Directory-record count is bounded by the directory extent; recursive path depth is capped at 16.
surfaces.allocation_time: Per-lookup directory storage is capped at 512 KiB; repeated path components can repeat those bounded scans.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Reader results fail closed; nk_iso_inspect reports malformed optional metadata without claiming executable support.

surfaces.max_input: Extent/buffer size supplied by the ISO path; SFO offsets and counts are checked against that extent.
surfaces.tables_nesting: Entry count and key/data table spans are extent-bounded; no recursive structure.
surfaces.allocation_time: Linear in the bounded SFO extent; fixed metadata fields prevent proportional host allocation.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Callers receive false on truncation, overlap, duplicate required keys, or invalid text; product inspection reports the boundary rather than fabricating metadata.

surfaces.max_input: Executable classification cap is 512 MiB; encrypted inner-image parsing is not implemented.
surfaces.tables_nesting: ~PSP segment count is 1..4; ~SCE and PBP are classification-only boundaries.
surfaces.allocation_time: Classification reads at most 128 bytes plus bounded ~PSP segment headers; no inner decrypt/decompress allocation occurs.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Encrypted containers remain explicitly unsupported; the clean-room loader refuses ~PSP before mutation or guest writes.
surfaces.gap: KIRK inner decryption/decompression is not implemented and is in the works under issue #295.

surfaces.tables_nesting: Program headers: at most 128 entries of exactly 32 bytes. Section headers: at most 65535 entries of exactly 40 bytes; preflight validates the table extent but does not consume section entries.
surfaces.allocation_time: Program headers use a fixed 4096-byte stack buffer; zero-filled classification scans at most 512 MiB in 8192-byte chunks.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Each candidate and the aggregate report are cleared before classification; malformed ELF becomes UNKNOWN and cannot be selected.

surfaces.boundary: Clean-room PRX ELF, program-header, and section-header walker
surfaces.max_input: 256 MiB in memory or from a host file; at most 4 PT_LOAD segments and 64 MiB aggregate guest image.
surfaces.tables_nesting: ELF16 program/section counts are input-bounded; exports and imports are each capped at 65536 entries.
surfaces.allocation_time: File and image allocations are capped; table and relocation work is linear in the capped input.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Parse and relocation failures discard scratch before guest writes. A callback failure after a later segment can leave earlier segment writes visible.

surfaces.max_input: 8-byte records contained in the 256 MiB PRX input; at most four segments.
surfaces.tables_nesting: Record count is stream_bytes/8; HI16 runs are scanned at most twice.
surfaces.allocation_time: Linear in the declared relocation stream; all sites are checked against scratch segment extents.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: A malformed record terminates parsing before the scratch image is committed.

surfaces.max_input: Packed commands and extensions contained in the 256 MiB PRX input; at most four segments.
surfaces.tables_nesting: Flag and kind widths are each 1..8 bits; combined widths are capped at 16 command bits.
surfaces.allocation_time: Linear in the declared packed stream; truncation, invalid indices, and out-of-range sites fail closed.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: A malformed command terminates parsing before the scratch image is committed.

surfaces.tables_nesting: JSON depth 16; modules 32, compatibility IDs 16, executable spans 64, device prefixes 16, feature requirements 64, dispatch aliases 32.
surfaces.allocation_time: AST allocation is bounded indirectly by the byte cap; duplicate-key rejection remains quadratic in unique keys within one object.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Schema validation completes before overlay publication; direct caller output structs are not a rollback mechanism for externally owned state.

surfaces.max_input: 262144 bytes each for package.json and build-report.json; embedded profile JSON uses the same cap.
surfaces.tables_nesting: JSON depth 16; package arrays have no schema-specific count cap beyond total bytes.
surfaces.allocation_time: Each AST is byte-bounded; executable hashing and image existence checks are linear but currently have no separate byte cap.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: NkRuntimePackageInfo is cleared on entry and populated only after every contract check passes.

surfaces.max_input: Experimental profile reads are capped at 262144 bytes; the cache manifest is a canonical serialization of an already validated manifest.
surfaces.tables_nesting: Inherits title-manifest limits; cache-only producer does not define an independent reader schema.
surfaces.allocation_time: Profile JSON is byte-bounded; cache replacement is staged and ownership-marked.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Private-file writes use temporary replacement; package promotion retains a rollback step.
surfaces.gap: The native package consumer is fuzzed, but the Python cache manifest producer has no dedicated seeded mutation harness; track under issues #316/#297.

surfaces.max_input: 512 MiB archive, 100000 files, 16 MiB string table, 256 MiB per entry, 512 MiB total expanded bytes.
surfaces.allocation_time: Archive, entry, total-expanded, nesting, and code-table budgets are explicit.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: The archive object is not published until all FST, name, span, and compressed-header checks pass.

surfaces.tables_nesting: At most NK_MAX_GAMES entries; each scalar parser writes only fixed-size fields.
surfaces.allocation_time: One bounded file allocation and a linear cursor walk.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Malformed input returns an error and invokes backup recovery, but entries appended before a later parse error are not rolled back inside the temporary library object.

surfaces.max_input: 2048-byte header; declared 32-bit stream extent must fit the source.
surfaces.tables_nesting: At most 119 stream entries fit the 2048-byte header; the implementation also rejects counts above 128.
surfaces.allocation_time: No stream-wide allocation at open; impossible timestamp normalization bases are refused before allocation.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Invalid headers, extents, stream tables, and presentation bases free the new producer and return NULL.

surfaces.max_input: PES packet length is 16-bit; each selected track buffers at most 4 MiB; queue depth is 8.
surfaces.tables_nesting: No recursive structure; 64 concurrent timestamp marks bound cross-packet AU ownership.
surfaces.allocation_time: Per-PES payload and per-track allocations are bounded; cumulative stream duration and total packet count are not bounded.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Failure is terminal and observable through stats. Cursor and counters can advance before a selected-track allocation fails, so the producer object is not rolled back.

surfaces.max_input: 4 MiB live track and 8 queued AUs per selected track.
surfaces.tables_nesting: No recursive structure; incremental scan state is retained across appends and compaction.
surfaces.allocation_time: Candidate scanning is incremental and linear in appended bytes; the no-AUD and compaction selftests pin the work bound.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Only complete bounded AUs enter the queue; queue backpressure stops parsing without dropping buffered bytes.

surfaces.boundary: Windows Media Foundation MPEG/H.264 demux seam
surfaces.max_input: 16 MiB unparsed PS buffer, 64 MiB demuxed ES, 1048576 ES chunks, four decoder instances.
surfaces.tables_nesting: Chunk table is explicitly capped; no recursive syntax nesting.
surfaces.allocation_time: PS, ES, and chunk buffers are capped; repeated demux loop work is linear in accepted input.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Failure poisons the decoder instance, but a failed feed can retain appended input and partial ES/chunk state until destruction.
surfaces.gap: The hostile campaign executes only with the Windows Media Foundation backend; Linux ASan/UBSan covers the portable producer and reports this seam as SKIP.

surfaces.max_input: Frame size 16..2824 bytes, 8192-byte resync window, 4 MiB track.
surfaces.tables_nesting: No recursive structure; incomplete frames remain buffered across PES boundaries.
surfaces.allocation_time: Frame and track sizes are bounded; resync scans at most the fixed 8192-byte window per extraction attempt.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Invalid frame-size fields fail terminally; complete frames are copied into bounded AU storage before queue publication.

surfaces.max_input: No public parser accepts PGF bytes in the public-safe tree.
surfaces.allocation_time: Immediate NULL/0 fail-closed result; no PGF allocation or scan.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: No font object or glyph state is published.
surfaces.gap: The lineage-sensitive PGF backend is excluded from public-safe builds and remains in the works under issue #313.
